title: Data Visualization Specialist
description: A deep, project-based roadmap for Data Visualization Specialist: Create analytical visuals with chart selection, dashboard design, accessibility, storytelling, D3, Power BI/Tableau, and stakeholder communication.

tree.name: Introduction to Data Visualization & Core Principles
tree.description: Establish a strong foundation by understanding the purpose, history, and fundamental principles of effective data visualization, the evolving role of a specialist, and key terminology.

children.name: Understanding Data, Data Types & Sources
children.description: Learn about different data types (quantitative, qualitative, categorical, ordinal), data structures (tabular, hierarchical, network, geospatial), common data sources (databases, APIs, files), and fundamental concepts of data granularity and cardinality relevant for visualization.

children.name: Foundational Principles of Effective Visualization
children.description: Explore foundational theories by pioneers like Edward Tufte (data-ink ratio, graphical integrity, chart junk) and Stephen Few (perceptual processing, visual analytics). Understand cognitive load, Gestalt principles of perception, and choosing appropriate visual encodings for clarity and impact.

children.name: Visual Encoding, Chart Typology & Selection
children.description: Master how different visual variables (position, color, size, shape, orientation, texture) encode data effectively. Learn to identify and select the most appropriate chart types (e.g., bar, line, scatter, treemap, heatmap, geospatial) for various data relationships and analytical goals, moving beyond default chart suggestions.

children.name: Data Visualization Ecosystem: Tools Overview & Setup
children.description: Get acquainted with the broad ecosystem of data visualization tools. This includes commercial BI platforms (Tableau, Power BI, Looker), open-source programming libraries (Python with Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly; R with ggplot2), and web-based frameworks (D3.js, Vega-Lite). Set up initial development environments for selected tools.

tree.name: Advanced Data Visualization Techniques & Tools
tree.description: Develop hands-on proficiency in creating sophisticated visualizations, designing impactful dashboards, and using industry-standard tools and programming languages to solve real-world analytical challenges.

Data Visualization with Python - Full Course for Beginners and Data Scientists

children.name: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) & Visual Discovery
children.description: Learn to use visualization as a primary tool for initial data exploration, identifying patterns, outliers, anomalies, and relationships. Understand how EDA informs subsequent data cleaning, feature engineering, and visualization design choices. Master techniques for univariate, bivariate, and multivariate visual analysis.

children.name: Data Preparation & Transformation for Visualization
children.description: Master techniques for cleaning, structuring, and transforming raw data into a suitable 'tidy' format for optimal visualization. Cover concepts like data shaping (pivoting/unpivoting), aggregation, joining/blending data from multiple sources, handling missing values, and creating calculated fields using various tools (e.g., Power Query, Tableau Prep) and languages (SQL, Python Pandas).

children.name: Advanced Chart Design & Customization
children.description: Dive deeper into choosing the right chart for complex data and specific messages. Master advanced design elements: effective color theory (sequential, diverging, categorical palettes), typography for readability, use of negative space, visual hierarchy, and annotations to enhance clarity and impact. Learn to avoid common pitfalls in chart design.

children.description: Learn principles of effective dashboard design, including layout strategies (e.g., F-pattern, Z-pattern), grid systems, responsive design for different devices, interactivity elements (filters, parameters, actions), guided analytics, and considerations for user experience (UX) to create intuitive and actionable dashboards that support decision-making.

Focus on audience analysis and call to action.
